q: A transformer is used to change the voltage of an alternating current. (2024)
e: A transformer steps up or steps down the voltage of an alternating current through electromagnetic induction.

q: In Myanmar, the prevalent AC line frequency is 50 Hz, while the standard voltage utilized for residential and commercial applications falls within the voltage of 220 V to 240 V. (2024)
e: Standard residential and commercial AC power in Myanmar operates at 50 Hz and 220 V to 240 V.

q: A transformer is used to change the voltage of an alternating current. (2024)
e: Transformers function specifically to alter the voltage of alternating current.

q: The currents flow in little circles in the iron core are eddy currents. (2024)
e: Eddy currents are circulating loops of electrical current induced within conductor cores.

q: Current flowing in power transmission line is alternating current. (2024)
e: Power grid transmission lines utilize alternating current for efficient long-distance voltage transformation.

q: Magnetic field strength is vector quantity. (2024)
e: Magnetic field strength possesses both magnitude and direction, making it a vector quantity.

q: A transformer is used to change the voltage of an alternating current. (2025)
e: A transformer alters AC voltage levels using mutual induction.

q: A transformer is used to change the voltage of a direct current. (2021)
e: A transformer operates only on alternating current (AC) because direct current (DC) does not create a continuously changing magnetic flux.

q: In an AC (alternating current) circuit, the current changes direction periodically. (2025)
e: Alternating current continuously reverses its direction of flow at regular intervals.

q: The current from the outlet of telephone charger is DC (direct current). (2021)
e: Phone chargers convert AC input from the wall power supply into DC output required by device batteries.

q: According to Lenz's law, the direction of induced current resists the change causing it. (2025)
e: Lenz's law dictates that an induced current always flows to oppose the magnetic flux change that produced it.

q: Transformers work on AC, but not on DC. (2021)
e: Transformers require time-varying magnetic fields produced by AC to induce voltage.

q: The frequency of AC current is 50 Hz in US and 60 Hz in Europe. (2025)
e: The standard frequency of AC current is 60 Hz in the United States and 50 Hz in Europe.

q: A transformer is used to change the voltage of an alternating current. (2025)
e: A transformer changes the magnitude of alternating voltage.

q: Only high current can be dangerous to human. (2025)
e: Both high current and high voltage present dangerous electrical hazards to humans.

q: The direct current is a steady unidirectional current. (2025)
e: Direct current maintains a constant direction of flow over time.

q: Lenz's law gives the direction of the induced emf. (2025, 2026)
e: Lenz's law determines the direction/polarity of induced electromotive force.

q: The lamps are connected in parallel in the lighting circuit. (2026)
e: Parallel connections allow each lamp to operate independently at full supply voltage.

q: The SI unit of magnetic flux density is the weber (Wb). (2026)
e: The SI unit of magnetic flux density is the tesla (T); the weber (Wb) is the unit of magnetic flux.

q: A great industrial current is known as direct current. (2026)
e: Alternating current (AC) is predominantly used for large-scale industrial electrical power.
